correctness.rationale: Both similarities are strictly decreasing functions 1/(1+t) of the minimum-unique/shared and total-unique/shared ratios, respectively; hence opposite strict order is equivalent to the negative product sign. Cases with a=0 have both similarities zero and never induce strict reversal. Independently enumerated all nonempty-site normalized Venn signatures (1,4,9,17 through gamma richness N=1..4), checked all unordered pair comparisons with exact Fraction arithmetic, finding zero, zero, zero, three reversals and exactly the three advertised pairs. For P_r=(1,0,r), Q_r=(r,1,1), differences J(Q_r)−J(P_r)=(r^2−2)/((r+1)(r+2))>0 for integer r>=2 while S(P_r)=1>S(Q_r), establishing infinite family. No extrapolation from the finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The smallest possible richness at which these widely used dissimilarity-based species ranking methods can disagree is a natural, ecologically interpretable finite cutoff; the complete three-signature first layer distinguishes perfectly nested communities from richer shared-but-nonnested pairs. The general order criterion and exact minimal witnesses can be used as test cases for cross-index comparisons. Although elementary, this is a motivated sharp classification rather than an arbitrary unmotivated numerical slice; it does not purport to settle measure selection.

final_claim: For positive shared species a,A and b<=c, B<=C, Jaccard J=a/(a+b+c) and Simpson turnover similarity S=a/(a+b) rank two site-pair signatures oppositely iff (b/a−B/A)((b+c)/a−(B+C)/A)<0. Under gamma richness <=3 per pair this never occurs; for <=4 there are exactly three normalized unordered reversal signature pairs, with an infinite nested/balanced family for r>=2.
limitations: Only pairwise binary incidence and per-pair regional richness bound, not abundance-weighted similarity or joint-isomorphism types of four communities.
No claim of ecological superiority or high mathematical depth.
